An agent built into a Foldkit application could not see what the person was looking at unless the application wrote its own projection of the Model, its own JSON encoding, and its own description for the model. Nothing kept other Model fields, such as drafts or session material, out of what it sent. DevTools MCP exposes the whole Model, but only on the development server.

AgentContext.define in foldkit/experimental takes the Model Schema, a field map in the shape of Schema.Struct, and a pure read callback. The result exposes Context (the Schema, for Command args and server decoding), fields, read, encode, and jsonSchema. The returned read keeps only the declared fields, even when the callback returns more of the Model, so Command args, Subscription dependencies, and the JSON from encode hold nothing else. jsonSchema is a standalone draft 2020-12 JSON Schema of the encoded context, with $schema, field annotations such as description, and $defs, for the agent's instructions or a tool definition.

The context reaches an agent through existing primitives. When update handles the Message that submits a prompt, it reads the context and returns a Command with the context as an argument, so DevTools history and Story tests show what each turn carried. A Subscription entry built from fields and read publishes the context to a server session; the Runtime compares Subscription dependencies with their Schema, so the entry restarts only when a declared field changes. Tests cover the projection, the removal of undeclared fields from read, Command args, and JSON, the standalone JSON Schema, a Story that attaches the context to a Command, and a running Program whose Subscription publishes at startup and after a declared change, but not after a change to another field.

Scope decisions: the context is read-only. Declaring Messages that an agent may send through the normal update is left for a follow-up. The website gains an Agent Context guide beside Machine.

The foldkit typecheck script now passes --checkers 1. The native compiler's result for packages/foldkit depends on its checker count (#1779): with the default four checkers, adding this module makes tsc report errors in unchanged files, such as block/fromAssembly.test.ts, experimental/query/query.test.ts, and runtime/applicationBlock.test.ts. With one, two, or three checkers the same tree typechecks clean. The check is about twice as slow. Remove the flag when the order dependence is fixed.

<!-- fork-migration: https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/pull/1580 -->
Replaces #1580. The commits are unchanged. This PR uses a personal fork to allow maintainer edits.

## Problem

A large client-rendered Foldkit application cannot activate an unseen route implementation after boot through the public runtime API. Loading a module in a Command does not install its synchronous update, view and Subscriptions. Restarting the Runtime loses the required lifecycle. This is an implementation contribution to #1559, not a claim that downstream performance budgets are already met.

## Decision

Add an optional runtime-owned `lazyComposition` channel to `Runtime.makeApplication` and `Runtime.makeElement`. Requested and accepted identities remain serializable Model data. The root reducer owns lifecycle acceptance; immutable implementation snapshots remain outside the Model. Successful code stays available for replay and return navigation. Root services, ManagedResources and application-wide Subscriptions retain their runtime lifetime; route Subscriptions follow complete build/key/request identity.

Restored accepted identity loads before first render. Import failures become identity-bearing Messages, retries need a new request identity, and failed resource provision crashes rather than publishing false readiness. Missing accepted implementations fail explicitly. Existing static configurations remain unchanged.

Scope: client rendering only. Hydration rejects this configuration; SSR/SSG resolves statically. This does not add a router, asset retention, modulepreload scheduler or automatic deployment swapping. The maintainer noted on #1559 that adoption may wait until v1; this PR is offered for review, not downstream adoption without a supported release.

## Verification

- Foldkit package and Vite plugin builds pass.
- Foldkit typecheck passes, including six negative undeclared-service cases and declared-Layer controls.
- Lazy lifecycle and inference suites: 15 tests pass across two files.
- Framework/application lint passes.
- Routing example typecheck passes after building its exported UI prerequisite.
- Built routing Chromium suite: four tests pass, one worker, zero retries.
- Real Vite manifest and emitted module graph prove Reports is absent from the initial static closure and dynamically loaded after boot, with one Foldkit and one Effect package root.
- Browser proof preserves the shell node, value and focus across delayed import; re-entry retains counter state without a second Reports request.
- Additional managed Chromium visual smoke: Reports loads, increments, returns Home and reopens with shell text and counter retained; no browser errors.

Public API documentation, an illustrative snippet, minor changeset, multi-entry example and production browser coverage are included.

## Publication gate notes

The initial local gate compared against a stale fork main and counted unrelated upstream commits. Local remotes now fetch canonical main while pushing the contribution to tao-io's fork. No upstream history was rewritten and no hook was bypassed.

The complete hook then passed formatting, changesets, lint, dead-code analysis, script typecheck and 190 script tests. Its prebundle check counted the test-only Deferred import despite the distribution compiler excluding test files. The scan now follows the compiler's test exclusion; it verifies the same 38 published runtime namespaces without adding test dependencies to consumer optimization.

The complete framework pre-push hook finished and published commit `0d02ada98` without bypass. Workspace builds, typechecks and test commands completed. Website Chromium returned 13 passed and one flaky existing Combobox navigation test (first attempt timed out waiting for the Documentation Combobox link, retry passed). This is not a clean browser-suite pass; its failure artifact is retained. The contribution's separate production routing check passed with retries disabled. Exact committed-diff review of both commits found no evidence-backed defects; the reviewer executed no checks.

Replaces #1768. The commits are unchanged. This PR uses a personal fork to allow maintainer edits.

A failing `Story.story` threw only the assertion that broke. The error did not say which step failed, which Messages ran before it, or how the Model reached the value under test, so the reader had to count steps by hand.

This change appends a step report to the thrown error. Every step is listed in order: `✓` ran, `✗` threw, blank never ran. A step that ran shows its Model changes as `path: before → after` lines and the Commands it emitted. The failed step shows the first error line, the current Model, and the pending Commands. An unresolved Command at the end of the story gets an `End` row.

Before:

```text
AssertionError: expected 2 to be 3 // Object.is equality

- Expected
+ Received

- 3
+ 2
```

```text
Error: Expected exactly these Commands:

    FetchCountById {"id":7}

But found:

    FetchCount
```

After:

```text
AssertionError: expected 2 to be 3 // Object.is equality

Story failed at step 4 of 5:

  ✓ 1 Given    { count: 0, log: [] }
  ✓ 2 Message  ClickedIncrement
               model     count: 0 → 1
  ✓ 3 Message  ClickedIncrement
               model     count: 1 → 2
  ✗ 4 Model
               error     expected 2 to be 3 // Object.is equality
               model     { count: 2, log: [] }
    5 Message  ClickedDecrement

- Expected
+ Received

- 3
+ 2
```

```text
Error: Expected exactly these Commands:

    FetchCountById {"id":7}

But found:

    FetchCount

Story failed at step 4 of 5:

  ✓ 1 Given                { count: 0, log: [] }
  ✓ 2 Message              ClickedIncrement
                           model     count: 0 → 1
  ✓ 3 Message              ClickedFetch
                           commands  FetchCount
  ✗ 4 Command.expectExact  FetchCountById { id: 7 }
                           error     Expected exactly these Commands:
                           model     { count: 1, log: [] }
                           pending   FetchCount
    5 Command.resolveAll   FetchCount → SucceededFetchCount { count: 1 }
```

Scope decisions:

- The original Error instance is kept and its message stays first; the report is added after it. Existing `toThrow('...')` checks and assertion diffs (`expected` / `actual`) keep working.
- `Story.steps` groups are flattened, so step numbers follow the order the steps run.
- Values print on one short line. Long strings and arrays are cut, and `Redacted` values print as their placeholder, never their content.
- Step descriptions are built only when a story fails. Command steps carry a description in a symbol-keyed property on the step function; the public step types are unchanged.
- `Scene` failures are left alone. The same report could apply there, but Scene has more step kinds (view queries, mounts), so I kept this change to Story.

Verified with new tests in `story.test.ts` (model failure, Command failure with a grouped setup, the end check, error compatibility, redaction and truncation), the full `foldkit` and `@foldkit/ui` suites, `tsc`, both oxlint configs, `oxfmt --check`, and the pre-push suite.

Foldkit had no primitive for data that a server pushes as a stream of changes, such as a shared board, a synchronized document, or an event-sourced read model. An application wrote its own Subscription, entry Messages, cursor bookkeeping, and reconnect logic, and a restart could apply an entry twice or lose one.

LiveQuery is a viewless Block in foldkit/experimental/liveQuery, modeled on Query. Each feed is selected by Schema args and retains AsyncData, the seq of the last applied entry, and a Connection state (Connecting, Live, Offline, Failed). Each entry carries the full state after the change, not a delta, so applying an entry replaces the retained state. An entry is applied only when its seq is greater than the cursor, and each applied entry emits AppliedEntry with the args, seq, maybePreviousCursor, and meta. A duplicate emits nothing and changes no data.

One Subscription streams every watched feed. Its dependencies change only when the feed set changes (watch, unwatch, pause, resume, or a feed that fails or ends), never on an applied entry. A restart resumes every streaming feed after its cursor in a new generation, and events from older generations are ignored. The trade-off: all feeds share one Stream, so a watch, an unwatch, or a feed that fails or ends reconnects every other streaming feed. No entry is lost as long as the handler opens the backend feed after the maybeAfter cursor it receives.

A feed is Connecting until its Stream delivers an entry in the current session, then Live. Loading means an open Stream with no entry yet; a feed with no data that pauses or ends returns to Idle. requestWatch takes an optional snapshot, so a hydrated feed starts as Success and resumes after the snapshot cursor. When a feed fails, loaded data becomes Stale and a feed with no data enters Failure, until requestResume retries it. sessionMessages builds the Messages of a feed's current session for tests.

The handler generator uses the same Layer machinery as Query, so the Services it or its Stream require become requirements of the completed Block. A declaration fixture shows that starting a Program without them is a type error. Omitting the handler gives a host contract completed with toLayer and provideHandlers.

Scope decisions: feeds are keyed by Schema args with the canonical key encoding KeyedQuery uses, which moves to the shared query internals. A sequence gap is applied, because the backend is the authority on which entries exist, and maybePreviousCursor lets a parent detect one. The website gains a LiveQuery guide beside Query.
title: feat(foldkit): add experimental LiveQuery for keyed live feeds

A page-owning view had no way to declare the page color scheme. An application that lets visitors choose light or dark could not render `<meta name="color-scheme">` for each request, so the first paint used the template's scheme, and the runtime never kept that element in sync with the Model.

Add `ColorScheme`, a Schema exported from `foldkit/html`, and an optional `colorScheme` field on `Document`. The runtime writes the value's content form, such as `light dark` for `LightDark`, to the `content` of `<meta name="color-scheme">` and reuses a served element. A later omission follows the canonical rule: it restores the served value or removes the element the runtime created. `Server.renderToString` returns the value as `colorScheme`. `Server.renderDocument` writes the meta after the title and before the `head` option markup and every stylesheet, and `injectIntoTemplate` replaces the `content` of a template's color-scheme meta.

The runtime matches served color-scheme, canonical, and og:url elements case-insensitively, as `injectIntoTemplate` does, so a served element whose identity attribute uses uppercase letters is reused instead of duplicated.

Document the field in the View, Server Rendering, and Runtime guides and in the generate-program skill, and name `colorScheme` in the `Server` error for a view rooted at a document-structure element.

This change does not move the website's `ApplyTheme` Command or `theme-init.js` to the new field, and it does not add `theme-color`. `injectIntoTemplate` leaves a template without a color-scheme meta unchanged, and the runtime creates the element after boot.

Fixes #1775.
title: feat(foldkit): add colorScheme to the view Document

Story message, Scene interactions and Scene.Subscription.emit stop a test while any Command is unresolved. Only interruptible and Interrupt Commands could stay pending. Closes #1769.

## What was wrong

A slow-phase measurement taken while the document is hidden includes the time the browser kept the tab throttled or descheduled. In production we saw `Update` reports of up to 176s for a Message whose update is cheap, all from tabs left open overnight. `onSlow` received no visibility information, so a reporter could not separate these from stalls the user saw without depending on when `reportSlowPhase` runs relative to the phase.

## What changed

- `SlowViewContext`, `SlowUpdateContext`, `SlowPatchContext`, and `SlowSubscriptionDependenciesContext` gain `isDocumentVisible: boolean`.
- `reportSlowPhase` builds a `SlowMeasurement` (`durationMs`, `thresholdMs`, `isDocumentVisible`) and passes it to `makeContext`. The five call sites in the runtime, renderer, and Subscription fibers spread it. `document.visibilityState` is read only when a phase exceeds its budget, so phases under budget cost nothing extra.
- The default `console.warn` appends "The document was hidden, so the browser may have throttled this work." when it was.
- The slow guide explains hidden-document inflation and lists the fields every context carries. The `slowConfig` snippet filters on `isDocumentVisible`.
- Changeset: `minor` for `foldkit`, since the public context types widen.

## Left alone

- No option to skip hidden-document phases. Filtering in `onSlow` covers it, and it is noted on the issue as a possible follow-up.
- Budgets, measured phases, and when a phase reports are unchanged.

## Verification

- `packages/foldkit`: `vitest run src/runtime/slow.test.ts` passes, 12 tests. New tests cover a visible and a hidden document across all four phases (stubbing `document.visibilityState`), and the default warning's hidden-document note.
- `packages/foldkit` typecheck passes.

Refs #1737. **Stacked on #1763.** GitHub can't base a fork PR on another fork branch, so this targets `codex/preview-followups` and includes #1763's commit. Review the second commit, `perf(foldkit): add Composition.assembleAs for generated Block contracts`.

This is the generated exact contract boundary the issue asked about. It converts only the Website root and Ui Blocks, as requested, and doesn't migrate other consumers.

## What was wrong

Every editor request in a file that depends on the root `ApplicationBlock` re-inferred the whole assembled implementation, including the `UiBlock` graph beneath it. Native TypeScript builds a fresh checker for each edited program, so none of that inference survives an edit.

That is why root completion after an edit took 5 to 6 s and root diagnostics about 5 s on 7.0.2. Root `update.ts`, `view.ts` and `composition.ts` paid most of the same cost.

## What changed

**1. `Composition.assembleAs<Implementation>()(implementation)`.** This is in `packages/foldkit/src/block/definition.ts`.

- It has a single generic signature, so there is no overload search.
- The completed Block type is computed from the contract, not inferred from the implementation.
- The supplied implementation still goes through `assembleBlock`'s `ValidateInit`, `ValidateView` and `ValidateAssembleBlockComposition`, plus a new `ValidateContractImplementation`.
- `ValidateContractImplementation` requires every public channel to equal the contract's channel in both directions, and rejects `any` and `never`.
- A contract that declares more than the implementation uses is rejected, and so is one that declares less.
- At runtime it is `() => composition.assembleBlock`, so emitted behaviour is identical.

**2. Two type-identity changes, both private.**

- **`replaceEffectsLayer`.** It moves from an inline generic function type into a named callable interface, `ReplaceEffectsLayer`. When relating an inferred Block to an independent contract, that inline signature alone cost 4.57M of a 5.15M relation. Named, the same relation costs about 0.58M, because the instantiations are interned. This only matters once a contract exists: in the contract-free base, renaming saves nothing measurable.
- **`in` variance annotations** on the seven private Html element function aliases.

**3. A contract generator and its witnesses**, all in `packages/website`.

- **`scripts/generate-block-contracts.mjs`** uses the TypeScript compiler API. It reads the registered Binding graph, Commands, Mounts and Schemas, never the `init`, `update`, `view` or `EffectsLayer` values. It writes `block.contract.ts`, `block.bindings.contract.ts` and `block.lifecycle.contract.ts` next to each converted `block.ts`.
- **Subscription message tuples** are emitted as `(typeof registry)[key]['messages']`, so the contract is exact on both 7.0.2 and 7.1.0-beta. A hand-written contract fails on beta with TS2375 because of readonly tuple inference.
- **`check:block-contracts`** regenerates in check mode, fails on stale output, then typechecks the Website plus `contract-witnesses/`. The Website `typecheck` now runs it.
- **The witnesses cover:**
  - a bidirectional member-wise check that each `assembleAs` result equals its contract, with non-`any` and non-`never` guards;
  - Binding channel witnesses;
  - a re-inferred `assembleBlock` witness for both Blocks;
  - stale-contract mutations, such as an added Service, a refined Message or a removed Binding;
  - `assembleAs` mutations against the real root and Ui graphs.
- **`watch:block-contracts`** regenerates on save. While generation is pending or failed, `block.generation-status.ts` flips to `false`, which makes every generated contract a type error instead of silently stale.

**4. Consumer shape.** Each converted `block.ts` changes like this:

```ts
const assembled = ApplicationComposition.assembleAs<ApplicationImplementation>()({ init, update, view, subscriptions, EffectsLayer })
export const ApplicationBlock: ApplicationContract = assembled
export type AssembledApplication = typeof assembled
```

Refs #1737. This is the smaller, standalone half of the investigation in that issue. The generated contract boundary is in a separate draft stacked on this one.

## What was wrong

`ValidHandlerKindContracts` builds a key-indexed map of every handler entry. Then, for each entry, it indexes that map and compares the entry against every entry under its key. The Website root assembly pays this for each handler kind on every editor check. In the root Block the map is formed and indexed over and over, although every entry that shares a finite key belongs to the same group.

## What changed

`ConflictingIndexedKeys` now compares entries once per finite key group, using `ConflictsWithinGroup` over a mapped type keyed by the index.

Open key spaces are the exception. A `string` or template literal handler name can hide a narrower literal key when indexed through `keyof`. If any entry's key is open (`{}` satisfies `Record<Key, unknown>`), the validator falls back to the original per-entry algorithm, now named `OpenKeyConflicts`. The key and contract equality checks are the same within each group.

An earlier version without the open-key fallback passed ordinary Website diagnostics but failed a broad-key equivalence oracle, so the fallback is required, not defensive.

## What stayed the same

- Accepted handler sets and conflict diagnostics are unchanged.
- No public API changes. The only exported type touched is `ValidHandlerContracts`, which is `@internal`.
- Budgets in `type-performance/budgets.json` are unchanged.

## Verification

Run on the base commit plus this change:

- `vitest run` in `packages/foldkit`: 3,572 passed, 1 skipped. That includes two new regressions for literal collisions beneath `string` and `` `Read/${string}` `` handler names.
- `pnpm --filter foldkit typecheck`, `check:block-type-performance` and `check:emitted-declarations` pass, as does the Website `tsc --noEmit`.
- **Equivalence oracle (not committed).** A type-level file with 576 cases compares `ValidHandlerContracts` against a verbatim copy of the original implementation. It covers broad, template, literal-union, scoped, same-kind, cross-kind, refined, `any`, `unknown` and `never` inputs across three owner IDs. Every case agrees.
  - Bypassing the open-key fallback makes the new regression tests fail.
  - Removing the conflict check makes the oracle fail.
  - 576 concrete cases are not a proof for every unresolved generic expression.
  - The file is 140 KB, so I left it out. Happy to add a trimmed version if you want it in the suite.

## Measurements

Compiler work, TS6 instantiation counts for root Block demand: **20.43M → 17.59M (−13.9%)**.

Native TypeScript 7.0.2, Website root `block.ts` diagnostics, median ms. This uses the issue's scope-root editor probe in diagnostics mode, with 3 alternating AB/BA pairs against the base in one session. All 6 sessions passed their guards.

body:
Three type-level encodings in the Block assembly path made the native TypeScript checker repeat work that it only needs once per call, and that work dominated editor requests on the Website root. Each change keeps the same acceptance and rejection outcomes; it changes how the checker reaches them.

`ValidHandlerContracts` compared every handler entry with every entry sharing its key, including the singleton groups, through two `Equal` checks per pair, and resolved the index's key set once per entry, so the scan was quadratic in the number of handler contracts. The check now resolves the key set once and runs the pairwise comparison only where the key's group is not identical to the entry itself. In the Website root completion this alias went from 0.48 s to under 0.1 s per request.

Six `assembleBlock` overloads carried their composition validation as a top-level intersection constituent. The checker instantiates a candidate's parameter type eagerly while checking arity and applicability, so those validations ran for candidates that then failed on `view?: never` or a missing `EffectsLayer`, and ran again on generic placeholders before inference. Those constituents now sit behind a conditional on the overload's own type parameter: a non-weak tuple shape test for the headless and default-EffectsLayer overloads, and a plain tuple guard for the remaining ones. A deferred conditional stays unevaluated while the type parameter is unresolved, a candidate whose shape cannot match returns `unknown` without instantiating the validation, and the tuple check type keeps the conditional from distributing over a union or `never` implementation. The selected overload still evaluates the full validation, so missing handlers, foreign owners, unregistered children, and the other rejection fixtures still fail.

`ConflictingDeliveryTags` recomputed `keyof OutgoingIndexes` for every incoming tag. The tag set is now a defaulted type parameter computed once per Composition.

Measured on the Website root `ApplicationBlock.` member completion with the pinned native TypeScript 7.0.2 on one idle macOS host (four root completions and two diagnostics runs per arm, interleaved in two blocks, medians): cold completion 5842 ms to 4947 ms, post-edit completion 5736 ms to 4872 ms, root diagnostics error appearance 5487 ms to 4722 ms. Emitted declaration acceptance and rejection fixtures, the foldkit test suite, and the Website typecheck pass unchanged. The type-performance ceilings drop from 1,152,618, 3,132,298, and 2,659,415 instantiations to 859,410, 1,609,445, and 386,770, the highest counts observed over six runs; the counts measured at the parent commit were 878,121, 1,975,974, and 911,507.

Each assembleBlock overload validated its candidate through a Readonly composition object built from that candidate's inferred implementation, so the local requirement validation ran once per overload candidate even when every candidate had resolved the same init, update, lifecycle registrations, EffectsLayer, and hostHandlers. ValidateImplementationChannels takes those channel types directly, so candidates that resolve the same channels share one cached validation and candidates whose channels are generic defer it. The composition-object chain (ValidateImplementationComposition, the LocalCompositionChannels dispatcher with its fast and fallback projections, HasCompleteLocalCompositionShape) is gone; one distributive InvalidHostDefinition and ValidateHostDefinitions pair serves the channel-keyed and the Block-keyed paths. requirements.test.ts pins the accepted channels, missing and unexpected host handlers, conflicting handler contracts, erased requirements, invalid host definitions, and the declared-Owner branch on ValidateImplementationChannels, and authoring.test.ts rejects the same cases through assembleBlock. Diagnostics for the rejected cases are byte-identical before and after.

BindingAt distributed a conditional type over Children[number] for every placement lookup, one structural check per registered Binding per lookup. It now reads BindingIndex, a key-remapped mapped type keyed by placement and built once per Composition. Placements that are not a single string literal go into one unindexed bucket that keeps the scan, and a non-literal lookup key scans every Binding as before, so the resolved Binding is unchanged for every input.

In an SSR app that installs Foldkit from npm, a normal reload after a dev server restart refused to hydrate the page until a hard reload. Vite serves Foldkit's build-token module from node_modules with ?v=<browserHash> and an immutable Cache-Control header, and the hash does not depend on the build id. The plugin compiled the id into that module as a literal, so the browser kept the id of an earlier dev server and Runtime.hydrate refused the page from the running one. A configured buildId or FOLDKIT_BUILD_ID that changed between restarts caused the same refusal.

In serve mode, the build-token transform in @foldkit/vite-plugin now replaces the placeholder with a binding imported from the plugin virtual module virtual:foldkit/development-build-id. The plugin loads that module with the id of the running dev server, which all of its environments share. Vite serves the module with no-cache and an ETag, so the browser revalidates it on each load. The plugin has no new public option, export, or type.

Build output keeps the inlined literal and does not import the virtual module. Each dev server without a configured id generates its own id, and a configured buildId or FOLDKIT_BUILD_ID takes priority over it. The import.meta.env.FOLDKIT_BUILD_ID define keeps its existing behavior: in serve mode it uses "development" when no id is configured. The foldkit package does not change.

body:
Query handles fetching and caching, but three common jobs still forced the application back to hand-written AsyncData code. This PR adds one feature for each, as requested in #1727. All three are additions. Existing `update`, `fold`, and `lift` calls compile and behave as they do on `main`.

### Write a mutation result straight into the cache

Why: when a save or create request returns the updated resource, the only way to show it was to fetch it again. The old value stayed on screen until that second request finished.

What: `setData` stores a value as `Success`. `updateData` changes the value Query already holds, for example to add a created post to a loaded list. Neither one fetches.

```ts
SucceededSavePost: ({ post }) =>
  Update.combine(model, [
    postDetails.setData({ args: { postId: post.id }, data: post }),
    posts.updateData(postList =>
      Array.map(postList, listedPost =>
        listedPost.id === post.id ? post : listedPost,
      ),
    ),
  ]),
SucceededCreatePost: ({ post }) =>
  posts.updateData(model, postList => Array.append(postList, post)),
```

How they behave:

- A write wins over a request that is still running. Query ignores that request's result when it arrives.
- `updateData` does nothing when there is no data yet (`Idle`, `Loading`, `Failure`), so the caller does not need to check first.
- `Refreshing` becomes `Success`, because the write replaces the refresh. `Stale` stays `Stale` and keeps its error, because the write does not mean a refresh succeeded.
- A KeyedQuery takes the entry's arguments with the value: `{ args, data }` and `{ args, toNextData }`. `setData` creates the entry if it does not exist.

### Build test fixtures with seed

Why: to start a test from loaded, failed, or refreshing data, a test had to build the Query Model by hand. That meant knowing its internal fields, its request counter, and how KeyedQuery turns arguments into keys.

What: `seed` builds a Query Model in any AsyncData state. A KeyedQuery's `seed` takes a list of entries and keys them the same way loading does. The API Cache Query fixtures now use it:

```ts
export const loadedPostsModel = modifyFields(loadingPostsModel, {
  posts: () => postsQuery.seed(AsyncData.Success({ data: fetchedPosts })),
})

export const failedFirstPostModel = modifyFields(loadedPostsModel, {
  postDetails: () =>
    postQuery.seed([
      {
        args: firstPostArgs,
        data: AsyncData.Failure({ error: 'The connection dropped.' }),
      },
    ]),
})
```

One rule to remember in tests: a seeded Model starts its request counter at 0. A seeded `Loading` or `Refreshing` value completes with generation 0, and the first request a test starts from a seeded Model has generation 1.

### React when a request result is accepted

Why: a parent sometimes needs to act after a request finishes, for example to load related data. Query told the parent nothing, so the only option was to give up Query and manage AsyncData directly.

What: `lift` takes an optional `foldOutMessage`. Query calls it with an `AcceptedFetch` message when it accepts a request's result, success or failure. A late result, or one replaced by a write or reset, triggers nothing. Here the parent loads the first post's details once the list arrives:

```ts
const prefetchFirstPost =
  (postList: ReadonlyArray<Post>): Update.Step<Model, Message> =>
  model =>
    Option.match(Array.head(postList), {
      onNone: () => ({ model }),
      onSome: ({ id }) => postDetails.loadIfMissing(model, { postId: id }),
    })

const posts = postsQuery.lift<Model, Message>({
  parentField: 'posts',
  toParentMessage: message => Message.GotPostsMessage({ message }),
  foldOutMessage: postsQuery.OutMessage.match<Update.Step<Model, Message>>({
    AcceptedFetch: ({ result }) =>
      Result.match(result, {
        onSuccess: prefetchFirstPost,
        onFailure: () => model => ({ model }),
      }),
  }),
})
```

Details:

- A KeyedQuery's `AcceptedFetch` also carries the entry's `args`.
- If the parent's response returns Commands that need services, pass them as the third type argument: `lift<Model, Message, HttpClient>`.
- Apps that use `Update.foldChild` directly can pass `updateWithOutMessage` as the child `update`. It settles results like `update` and also returns `AcceptedFetch`.

### Docs and tests

The Query guide gains a section for each feature with a snippet. New unit tests cover each operation, including results that arrive late or after a write, and a type test checks that service requirements reach the lifted `fold`.

Refs #1727

Server rendering spends most of its time checking the page it just built, not building it. Building the HTML string is fast. The time goes into what Foldkit does next: before `renderToString` returns, and again in `injectIntoTemplate`, it checks that a browser would read that HTML back as exactly the page the view described.

1. **Each check needs a full parse.** HTML is forgiving and quietly repairs bad markup. An unclosed `<textarea>` from an `h.InnerHTML` fragment can swallow the rest of the page. A stray `<body>` tag gets moved somewhere else, and a `<base>` tag changes every link. If the browser's tree does not match what Foldkit rendered, hydration attaches to the wrong nodes. The reliable way to catch this is to run a real HTML parser, parse5, over the whole string and inspect the tree it builds.
2. **The checks did not share all of their work.** #1659 let the fragment checks share one tree per scripting mode. The closes-cleanly check still parsed the root separately, with a trailing sentinel comment, and every shared tree was still built twice, once with scripting enabled and once with it disabled, because `<noscript>` content parses differently in the two modes. A page rendered with `renderToString` and placed with `injectIntoTemplate` was parsed whole 14 times per request, and each trusted `h.InnerHTML` fragment 3 more times.
3. **Server-side syntax highlighting exposed it.** loomframework.com started highlighting its code on the server, so every token arrives as its own `<span>` and a code-heavy page carries tens of thousands of nodes. The largest is 553 KB. One parse of it takes about 30 ms, and the checks took about half a second of every request for that page.

This change keeps every check and every error message, and shares the parses instead:

- The closes-cleanly check parses the root with its sentinel once per scripting mode, and the other root checks run on those same trees. A sentinel that survives as the last top-level node was parsed after everything the root opened had closed, so detaching it leaves exactly the tree the root markup parses to on its own. Markup that contains the sentinel's own text could leave its copy in place of the appended one, so that markup is parsed again without the sentinel, as before.
- parse5 reads the scripting flag only when it meets a `<noscript>` start tag, so markup without the text `<noscript` (in any letter case) parses identically in both modes. Every check now parses such markup once and walks the shared tree once. Text that mentions `<noscript` only inside an attribute or a comment takes the two-parse path, which costs a parse and never skips a check.

When neither the rendered markup nor the template contains `<noscript>`, a request now parses the whole page 6 times instead of 14, and each `h.InnerHTML` fragment twice instead of three times. A `<noscript>` in the template alone brings the count to 8. The rendered and injected HTML is unchanged.

Deliberately left alone:

- The document-structure check keeps its own parse. It parses the markup inside a whole probe document, because a fragment parse silently drops the `<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>` and `<frameset>` tags the check exists to catch.
- `injectIntoTemplate` still repeats the checks `renderToString` already ran on the same HTML. Skipping them safely needs the validation handoff #1657 describes, which is a separate change.
- The `h.InnerHTML` context check keeps its own parse. It parses each fragment under the element the page parse produced, with that element's attributes, while the reserved-content check parses it before serialization under a bare element named by the view. The two contexts can differ.

Refs #1657

With the patch, the same filter produced 0 additions, 729 removals, elementCount 0, and 9/6,530 dirty objects.

### Change
- Lazily create next-key membership only in the existing keyed-lookup path.
- Defer removals for previous children absent from the next list, then flush them in original index order.
- Preserve existing endpoint fast paths and retained-child matching/order.
Reproduces with any keyed list filtered to an ordered subsequence (e.g. table filtering).

### Production benchmark
1k keyed table, Event Timing and scripting med/p95 in milliseconds, interleaved origin/patch with 10 pairs per group:

| CPU | Action | Origin Event | Patch Event | Origin script | Patch script |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1x | Cell | 56/72 | 60/64 | 4.66/7.43 | 4.66/5.56 |
| 1x | Filter | 120/152 | 80/96 | 35.99/40.31 | 27.10/32.86 |
| 1x | Select | 32/40 | 36/56 | 5.48/11.38 | 6.18/8.88 |
| 4x | Cell | 252/320 | 236/288 | 23.07/33.96 | 19.61/33.97 |
| 4x | Filter | 472/— (n=9) | 312/328 | 132.70/163.22 | 105.86/120.66 |
| 4x | Select | 92/96 | 84/112 | 26.54/34.54 | 24.96/36.14 |

The 10k filter measurements below are from the prior separate-batch run, not the ABAB rerun: Event Timing was 832→352ms nominal and 4,784→1,392ms at 4x; scripting was 211.35→149.15ms and 1,054.09→586.96ms.

The temporary key-lookup counter was 0 for cell/select at both 1k and 10k (filter: 721 at 1k, 6,553 at 10k). The earlier separate-batch 1k nominal cell delta did not recur under ABAB: scripting medians were 4.66ms for both revisions. Cell/select never entered the changed branch. The 1k cell A/A control showed origin-server median differences of 8ms Event Timing and 0.83ms scripting; paired script differences had a 1.43ms median absolute gap.

Random shuffle was within Chromium noise (2.6% delta versus a 4.7% noise band); Happy DOM was 5.5% slower, outside its 3.5% noise band.

Pre-push lint, format, build, typechecks, and workspace tests completed. Website E2E completed with 15 passed and 3 flaky (accessibility runtime load, combobox navigation, VirtualList end-anchor assertion).

## Changes since the previous preview

The previous preview is `1f6776fa7ececa766188df5201eefec6ba781b5d`. It already uses `Composition.prepareBlock`, checked `Block.assemble(prepare)` exports, the `Definition.make*` factories and `Program.make` or `Program.makeElement`.

### Required migrations

- Pass a producer callback to `Definition.makeCommandsStep` and `Definition.makeOutMessageStep`. Use `() => value` for fixed output, a Model-aware callback when needed, or `.fromMessage` for a payload-only producer.
- Replace callback-authored `Composition.makeUpdate` calls with an exhaustive Model-first handler record. Use `makeUpdate({})` for message-free or routed-only Compositions and `makeUpdate.withContext(context => handlers)` when dispatch context is required.
- Reserve `layer` as the aggregate key of a closed, all-attached ManagedResource registry. Mixed or host-owned registries keep explicit providers.
- Handle DragAndDrop's `StartedKeyboardDrag` and `ChangedKeyboardTarget` OutMessages in exhaustive policies. Custom keyboard-move handlers and manually constructed result Messages must echo the invocation's `keyboardDragGeneration`; the public Story helper derives it from the selected pending Command.
- If the application uses keyed Command interruption, check its cancellation policies. `toKey` now receives only the own fields selected by `keyFields`; preserve precise selected fields in extracted policy annotations, handle uncertain fields as optional in broad policies and narrow mixed policy unions before construction. See [keyed interruption](https://foldkit-website-preview-ky42cyp8l-devin-jamesons-projects.vercel.app/core/commands#choosing-an-interruption-key).
- Preserve connected result channels. Use Definition-owned local Steps when one handler mixes local results with connected Binding recipes, and retain or handle an operation's parent OutMessage instead of discarding it.

Ordinary raw-only handlers can still return results directly. Existing checked Block assembly and correctly wired child graphs do not need to be rebuilt.

### Behavior and safety fixes

- Per-Message handler records retain each operation's Commands, requirements and OutMessages. Connected-Step and Program checks reject demonstrated channel and requirement loss while retaining the documented TypeScript erasure limits.
- Effect DateTime and TimeZone values work in nested ViewInputs while application callbacks remain rejected. `Update.withOutMessage` keeps its OutMessage through supported connected combinations.
- A second `OnMount` on one element now throws during VNode construction and names both Mounts before either handler starts.
- Browser playground manifests preinstall a compatible Rolldown WASI binding and runtime pair, and the deployed SSR/SSG checks wait for hydration within their existing timeout.
- The Workspace example exercises retained per-entity editing, optimistic board changes, persistence, notifications and accessible Foldkit UI controls. Runtime and editor measurements retain their published workload and source limits; main remains faster in the recorded rendering screen.

### Optional conveniences

- Focused field, Command and OutMessage Step producers support Model-aware callbacks and payload-only `.fromMessage` forms.
- `makeMapBinding`, `makeVariantBinding`, and the set, append and insert Binding initialization helpers cover proven storage shapes while leaving custom parent transitions explicit.
- Closed, fully attached ManagedResource registries now expose `.layer`, matching the existing Subscription registry aggregate. Test helpers add identity-based Command argument inspection, headless child facts and explicit concurrent Message, Subscription and pending-Command delivery.
- The Block customization guide groups factories, checked alternate embedded views, view inputs, child attributes, handler replacement and wrapper Blocks without adding arbitrary completed-Block transforms.

## Previous verified preview

The previous snapshot remains available at [commit `1f6776fa7ece`](https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/commit/1f6776fa7ececa766188df5201eefec6ba781b5d), with its [immutable documentation](https://foldkit-website-preview-jlwvct0dx-devin-jamesons-projects.vercel.app/) and [package manifest](https://foldkit-website-preview-jlwvct0dx-devin-jamesons-projects.vercel.app/preview-release.json).

## Bonus prompt: understand your migrated app


## Why Foldkit is making this change

**Build applications from Blocks. Fold their updates into a single application Model.**

Blocks give features ownership of their state, behavior, optional views, effects, and public operations. A counter and a large website follow the same architecture.

Parents connect Blocks through Bindings. Foldkit handles repetitive child initialization, Message routing, and lifecycle wiring. You decide which children exist, how they coordinate, and what your application does. TypeScript checks those connections and dependencies as the application is assembled.

**This is a breaking release combining Block composition and handler Layers.**

## What changes

### 1. Reusable features become checked Blocks

A feature exports a completed value such as `SearchBlock`. Parents use its Model Schema, connect it through a Binding, and use the Binding's operations and view. The feature's implementation stays internal.

Authoring has three stages:

1. **Definition** establishes identity, contracts, and early authoring helpers.
2. **Composition** registers children and Mounts and authors init, update, and view.
3. **Assembly** prepares a checked draft through `Composition.prepareBlock`, then exports the completed Block through `Block.assemble(prepare)` with its checked `FromAssembly*` annotation. The explicit Model/producer boundary keeps parent Schema access from demanding full implementation inference.

These stages build configuration. Runtime constructs Layers and executes effects later. Even a feature without children or Mounts uses a Composition.

Preparation requires each handler to be supplied locally or delegated through `hostHandlers`. Delegated requirements remain visible to the parent.

### 2. Parent-owned Bindings connect children once

Bindings describe a child's Model storage, identity, initialization, Message delivery, and OutMessage policy.

- Direct-field shorthands cover required and optional children.
- Custom readers and writers express parent policy; keyed Bindings preserve instance identity, membership, and order.
- Registered children contribute their handlers and lifecycle registrations automatically.
- Child presence and Subscription-only activation remain separate policies.

Composition derives qualified effect identities and checks child and Mount registrations, including uses through operations, initialization, nested views, and supplied content.

#### Message unions and updates contain local facts

Parents previously declared and routed child wrappers alongside their own facts:

**Before**

```ts
const Message = defineMessageUnion({
  ClickedSave: {},
  GotCounterMessage: { message: Counter.Message },
})

const update = (model: Model, message: Message) =>
  Message.match(message, {
    ClickedSave: () => ({
      model,
      commands: [SavePanel()],
    }),
    GotCounterMessage: ({ message }) =>
      foldCounter(model, message),
  })
```

**After**

```ts
const Message = defineMessageUnion({
  ClickedSave: {},
})

const update = PanelComposition.makeUpdate({
  ClickedSave: model => ({
    model,
    commands: [SavePanel()],
  }),
})
```

Your update describes your feature's behavior; Composition routes child Messages. Model, Message, and Command requirements are inferred. Parent coordination uses Binding OutMessage policies and public operations.

`PanelComposition.Message` provides the complete dispatch Schema, including generated child-routing Messages, for Runtime and DevTools.

#### Child wiring before and after

The old parent also repeated its child relationship in the fold and view:

**Before**

```ts
const foldCounter = Update.foldChild({
  update: Counter.update,
  read: (model: Model) => Option.some(model.counter),
  write: (model, nextCounter) =>
    modifyFields(model, { counter: () => nextCounter }),
  toParentMessage: message => Message.GotCounterMessage({ message }),
})

const view = Submodel.defineView<Model, Message>((model, h) =>
  h.submodel({
    slotId: 'counter',
    model: model.counter,
    view: Counter.view,
    toParentMessage: message => Message.GotCounterMessage({ message }),
  }),
)
```

**After**

```ts
const CounterBinding = PanelDefinition.makeBinding(CounterBlock, {
  field: 'counter',
})

const PanelComposition = PanelDefinition.makeComposition({
  bindings: [CounterBinding],
})

const view = PanelComposition.makeView((model, h) =>
  h.block(
    CounterBinding.embedView({
      slotId: 'counter',
      model: model.counter,
    }),
  ),
)
```

One Binding now supplies both update and view wiring.

### 3. Composition assembles child initialization

Binding policies choose child initializer arguments and which optional or keyed instances initially exist. Parent init supplies shared child-initialization context and its own fields. Composition places the child Models and collects their Commands.

Additional startup policy uses ordinary Steps. `Update.combineSteps` orders pure transitions; it does not guarantee sequential Command completion. There is no separate Runtime boot phase.

#### Initialization before and after

For example, the old Counters application initialized each child in its parent:

```ts
export const init = () => ({
  model: {
    rows: [
      { id: 'counter-0', counter: Counter.init },
      { id: 'counter-1', counter: Counter.init },
      { id: 'counter-2', counter: Counter.init },
    ],
    nextRowId: 3,
  },
})
```

The Counters Binding declares the initial instances. Parent init supplies only its own fields:

```ts
export const init = ApplicationComposition.makeInit(() => ({
  model: { nextCounterId: INITIAL_COUNTER_COUNT },
}))
```

### 4. Public child operations go through Messages

Declare a Block's public API under `operations`. Binding methods produce parent Steps that enter the child's update.

Names distinguish actions from notifications:

- `requestCloseMenu` constructs `Message.RequestedCloseMenu`.
- `informJoined` constructs `Message.InformedOfJoin`.

Parents change child state through these operations. Read-only selectors remain ordinary helpers.

#### Parent operations before and after

Search previously needed a separate adapter to close its Dialog:

**Before**

```ts
const closeDialog = Update.foldChildStep({
  update: Dialog.close,
  read: (model: Model) => Option.some(model.dialog),
  write: (model, nextDialog) =>
    modifyFields(model, { dialog: () => nextDialog }),
  toParentMessage: message => Message.GotSearchDialogMessage({ message }),
  foldOutMessage: foldSearchDialogOutMessage,
})
```

**After**

```ts
const closeDialog = DialogBinding.requestClose()
```

The Step preserves the Binding's Model mapping, Command lifting, OutMessage policy, and instance identity, and composes through `Update.combineSteps`.

### 5. Effect handlers become Layer recipes

Commands, Subscriptions, Mounts, and ManagedResources separate their contracts from handler construction.

- Attach a canonical constructor through `handler` and compose its `.layer` into `EffectsLayer`.
- Use the original definition's `.toLayer` for an external implementation.
- The root provider supplies ordinary Services. Service requirements and constructor errors remain typed through assembly.

Constructors capture stable dependencies. Shared infrastructure such as RPC clients belongs in application Service Layers; application state stays in the Model.

#### Command handlers before and after

This draft-saving Command illustrates the split. The Message constructors and `DRAFT_STORAGE_KEY` are assumed below.

**Before**

```ts
const StoreDraft = Command.define('StoreDraft', {
  args: { contents: Schema.String },
  messages: [Message.CompletedStoreDraft, Message.FailedStoreDraft],
  execute: ({ contents }) =>
    Effect.gen(function* () {
      const store = yield* KeyValueStore.KeyValueStore

      yield* store.set(DRAFT_STORAGE_KEY, contents)
      return Message.CompletedStoreDraft()
    }).pipe(
      Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(Message.FailedStoreDraft())),
    ),
})
```

**After**

```ts
const StoreDraft = DraftEditorDefinition.makeCommand('StoreDraft', {
  args: { contents: Schema.String },
  messages: [Message.CompletedStoreDraft, Message.FailedStoreDraft],
  handler: function* () {
    const store = yield* KeyValueStore.KeyValueStore

    return ({ contents }) =>
      store.set(DRAFT_STORAGE_KEY, contents).pipe(
        Effect.as(Message.CompletedStoreDraft()),
        Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(Message.FailedStoreDraft())),
      )
  },
})

const EffectsLayer = StoreDraft.layer
```

Pass `EffectsLayer` to `DraftEditorComposition.prepareBlock`, then create the completed Block with `Block.assemble(prepare)` and its checked export annotation. The handler constructor captures the storage Service when Runtime builds its Layer; each invocation receives fresh `contents`. The Program supplies storage separately:

```ts
const ApplicationLayer = BrowserKeyValueStore.layerLocalStorage

Runtime.run(program.provide(ApplicationLayer))
```

Update continues to return `StoreDraft({ contents })`.

#### Implementation dependencies stay with the handler

Consider a `CreateRoom` Command whose handler uses `RoomsClient`. Later, the handler also needs `Telemetry`.

| Boundary | Handler requirements carried directly by the Command | Handler supplied through a Layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Update and parent folds | Requirements change from `RoomsClient` to `RoomsClient \| Telemetry` | Continue to require the declared `CreateRoom` handler |
| Application assembly | Supplies the implementation Services | Checks the handler Layer's new `Telemetry` requirement |

Adding `Telemetry` changes the handler Layer's requirements while update keeps the same `CreateRoom` contract. Missing Services remain visible in the application's requirements.

Ordinary application execution tests should keep the real handler and replace its underlying Services. Whole-handler replacement remains available for host implementations and deliberately controlled runtime scenarios.

The cost is explicit Layer composition; it makes missing implementations and Services visible before execution.

### 6. Construction does not change operation lifetimes

| Responsibility | Lifetime |
| --- | --- |
| Application Services and handler construction | One Runtime start and its application Scope |
| Command work | Each execution, including its interruption |
| Subscription Stream | Its active registration and dependency policy |
| Mount acquisition | The mounted element |
| ManagedResource handle | Its active Model-driven acquisition Scope |

Closes #1016 for `makeElement` and `embed`.

## What was wrong

Only `makeApplication` could adopt a server-rendered root. `embed` always started in `Fresh` mode, so markup rendered for a `makeElement` program was thrown away and rebuilt. A page with two stamped roots was also refused, because every stamped root counted as a page-owning application.

## What changed

- `renderToString` takes an `isEmbedded` option. It adds a `data-foldkit-embed` stamp beside `data-foldkit-app`. The `runtimeId` must equal the `id` of the container the client gives `makeElement`.
- `embed(program, { isHydratable: true, buildId? })` adopts the container when it carries the stamp. The program keeps the existing nodes and gets its Flags from the payload whose runtime id matches the root. Each root reads its own payload.
- `makeApplication` and `Runtime.hydrate` do not count roots with the embed stamp. One page holds any number of embedded roots beside at most one page-owning application. Two page-owning roots are still refused.
- A container without a stamp builds fresh from the `flags` Effect passed to `embed`, as before.
- Mismatch healing and the build id check are the ones `Runtime.hydrate` uses. `__hydrateVNode` is untouched.
- The stamp is looked up after any previous embed has torn down. A dispose followed by a fresh `embed` finds the stamp already consumed and builds fresh.
- `embed` without `isHydratable` behaves as it did.
- `injectIntoTemplate` refuses markup rendered with `isEmbedded`, and no longer counts embedded roots as page-owning when it places an application.

The API change is one option on `embed`, one option on `renderToString`, and one exported type, `EmbedHydrationOptions`. There are no new functions.

## What I left alone

- A `makeApplication` program cannot adopt a root through `embed`. It throws, and points to `Runtime.hydrate`.
- `injectIntoTemplate` still places the page-owning application only. The host puts an embedded root where its container belongs.
- The view of an embedded program is a plain `Html`, but `renderToString` takes a config whose view returns a `Document`. The server wraps it as `{ title: '', body }`. I did not add a second render function.
- Error messages that say `Runtime.hydrate` are unchanged, and an embed refusal reuses them where the cause is shared.

## How I checked it

- New `embedHydration.test.ts` (12 tests): two embedded roots adopt and keep node identity, each reads its own Flags payload, a tampered text node heals in place, an unstamped container builds fresh, a stamped sibling that belongs to another program is left alone, an application plus an embedded root on one page, two page-owning roots are still refused, build id skew contains the page, a page-owning stamp passed to `embed` is refused, a stamp that differs from the container id is refused, `embed` without `isHydratable` rebuilds as before, and a `makeApplication` program throws.
- One new test each in `server.test.ts` and `template.test.ts`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/foldkit`: 2968 passed, 1 skipped. Before the change: 2954 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/foldkit`, `oxlint --disable-nested-config packages/foldkit/src`, `pnpm lint:applications` and `oxfmt --check` pass.
- Chromium (Playwright), one host page with two server-rendered panels and a built client bundle: both roots and their input and count nodes are the same nodes after `embed`, 0 console warnings or errors, the page is not `inert`, typed input and focus survive a click, and only the clicked panel updates. With `isHydratable` off, the same nodes are replaced.

The full `pnpm pre-push` suite passes, including `check:dead-code`, the build and the website end-to-end pass. I ran it on Node 25 with `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage`, because Node 25's built-in `localStorage` shadows the jsdom one in the devtools tests. That is unrelated to this change.

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Should an embedded refusal contain the whole page, as `hydrate` does? A stale embedded widget makes the whole body `inert`. A narrower option is to contain only the root. I kept the existing behavior.
2. Is the stamp-equals-container-id rule right? It keys each root without a new lookup, and it forces the server and client to agree on the id. The alternative is to find the root by `runtimeId` and let the container differ.
3. Is `isEmbedded` on `renderToString` the right place for the marker, or should a dedicated render function for `makeElement` programs own it?
4. Should `embed` of a `makeApplication` program hydrate too? I left it out because such a program owns document metadata and navigation listeners.
5. Is the `isHydratable` option name right on `embed`? It matches the server option, but it reads as a request more than a fact.
title: feat(foldkit): hydrate server-rendered roots in Runtime.embed

Menu and Listbox decided that a keydown typed a character by looking at `event.key` alone: any key one character long started a typeahead search. Make `Html`, Scene elements, and `Attribute` opaque public types. Today `Html` is Snabbdom's `VNode | null` and every attribute constructor returns its tagged payload, so fields such as `sel`, `data`, `children`, `elm`, and `_tag` are public API in practice, and any change to how the renderer represents a view is a breaking change for applications. After this change, code outside Foldkit can still build, compose, pass, return, and null-check views and attributes, but it can no longer read or forge their representation. Nothing changes at runtime.

`Html` is now `HtmlNode | null`, where `HtmlNode` is a type-only brand, and `createLazy`, `createKeyedLazy`, `Submodel.View`, `defineView`, and `h.submodel` are typed with `Html`. The renderer still builds and patches Snabbdom nodes. The conversions live in one internal module and are identity functions, and the element and attribute build paths use erased type assertions only, so they make no new calls.

`Attribute<Message>` is now `ElementAttribute<Message> | InnerHtmlAttribute`. Each `HtmlBuilder` attribute constructor returns `ElementAttribute<Message>` when it carries a Message, `ElementAttribute<never>` when it does not, and `InnerHtmlAttribute` for `h.InnerHTML`. A textarea still rejects `h.InnerHTML`, and an attribute built for another Message type is still rejected. Custom element property and event factories return `ElementAttribute<Message>`, and `ChildAttribute` is opaque.

Scene's rendered tree and the elements its queries find are the new opaque `Scene.Element`, which `find`, `findAll`, `textContent`, `attr`, the `getBy*` functions, the Locators, and `sceneMatchers` take and return. Scene also gains `toHaveKey(key)`, in `Scene.expect` and in the Vitest matchers. Keys are authored view data (`h.keyed`, `h.Key`), and with opaque elements a test has no other way to assert one. The Scene guide documents the matcher. The website guides and snippets, the API reference, the `generate-program` skill, and the copy of the slow warnings example call what views return `Html` and describe the renderer's internals without naming its node type.

This is a breaking change at the type level only, shipped as a minor release while Foldkit is pre-1.0. Code that reads node or attribute fields, narrows attributes by `_tag`, inspects a `ChildAttribute`, or builds these values by hand no longer compiles, and should read through Scene queries and matchers instead. No example, `@foldkit/ui` component, or DevTools source needed a change. The DOM state parity gate script reads the data of the element its parity cases build, and now does so through Foldkit's internal conversion from the build output.

Tests outside the `foldkit` package that read these representations now use public APIs:

- The `@foldkit/ui` listbox tests read attributes through Scene.
- The website's playground preview test asserts keys with `toHaveKey`.
- The `@foldkit/markdown` view tests render through Scene.
- The `@foldkit/ui` Dialog tests assert on rendered elements. The Escape mapping, native cancel suppression, and the OnUnmount backstop gating moved to the Dialog runtime tests, which observe them in a running program.
- The `viewIdentity.test.ts` files in `@foldkit/ui` and `@foldkit/devtools` are removed, since they read `identity` off a node and the Vite plugin's view identity tests already cover the transform.

Related: #1604.

Closes #1606
Closes #761

A URL that ends in `#` or `?` parsed the same as one without the separator. `Url.fromString('https://app.example.com/docs#')` gave `hash: Option.none()`, and `Url.toString` then dropped the `#`. The runtime's link click, popstate, and programmatic navigation listeners did the same, so update could not tell a click on `<a href="#">` from a click on a link to the bare page. The HTML Standard sends an empty fragment to the top of the document, so applications need that difference.

Both paths read `URL.search` and `URL.hash`, which return `''` for a missing part and for an empty one, and then turned `''` into `None`. The serialized `href` keeps a lone `?` or `#`, so the parse now takes the query and the fragment from it and keeps an empty one as `Option.some('')`. The listeners use the same conversion as `Url.fromString`, through a new internal `fromWhatwgUrl`, so a cold load and a later navigation parse a URL the same way. That conversion splits the `href` at the first `#` and at the first `?` before it. The listeners already kept a second `?` in the query and a second `#` in the fragment, and splitting at every separator would have cut both. `Url.fromString` used to cut them, so it now keeps them too. That is the bug reported in #1496.

This is breaking. Code that passes `url.hash` to a selector must handle `''`, because `document.querySelector('#')` throws. The website now scrolls to the top for an empty fragment and skips the anchor scroll on a cold load. Code that reads `url.search` through `URLSearchParams` or a Foldkit route parser needs no change.

The listeners no longer use `StringExt.stripPrefixNonEmpty`, so the internal helper and its tests are removed.

The DevTools bridge answered `RequestDispatchMessage` and `RequestDispatchMessages` as soon as it had handed each Message to the queue. It could not see when the runtime dropped a Message, so it reported history indices that no entry would ever occupy. An agent staging state against a crashed tab was told its Messages were accepted while the application did not change. This happened in three cases:

- The runtime had already crashed or been disposed.
- Update threw on the dispatched Message.
- The runtime crashed or was disposed while the Message waited in the queue, for example behind a drain deferred to the next task.

The queue now numbers Messages in arrival order and counts the ones update processes. `enqueueMessagesAndAwaitProcessing` enqueues a batch in one synchronous step, so no other Message lands between its entries, and waits until each one is processed or dropped. The drain, the crash path in the renderer, and the queue's finalizer settle the waiting callers. The bridge's `dispatch` fails with `RuntimeStopped`, which carries how many Messages update processed, and the bridge answers with `ResponseError` instead of an index. When the runtime stops partway through a batch, the error says how many Messages update processed and gives their predicted history indices.

Messages excluded with `excludeFromHistory` still run update without a history entry, so their predicted indices stay empty. Both dispatch tool descriptions now say so. Expressing that per entry in the response needs a protocol change, which this change leaves out.

Part of #827. This change covers case 1. Case 2 (excludeFromHistory) stays open for a maintainer decision.
title: fix(foldkit,devtools-mcp): report DevTools dispatch that update never processes

Machine accepts any string literal as a state or Message tag, but toMermaid() put each tag into the stateDiagram-v2 source as written. A state named Not Asked became two states, a Message tag with a semicolon or the words direction TB lost its label, and a state named after a Mermaid keyword such as Note, Default, or Class stopped the diagram from parsing.

A state tag that is a plain identifier Mermaid cannot mistake for its own syntax is still its own state identifier, so most diagrams do not change. That excludes Mermaid keywords, the root_start and root_end start and end nodes, tags that start with an underscore, which Mermaid's Markdown labels read as emphasis, and tags that start with TB, BT, RL, or LR in any case, which Mermaid joins to a previous line ending in direction. Any other state tag gets an identifier built from the hexadecimal code points of the tag, under a state_ prefix that plain tags cannot use, and the tag becomes the display label through a state declaration. State and Message labels escape every character other than letters and digits as a Mermaid entity code. An empty Message tag omits the transition label, and an empty state tag shows a zero-width space, because Mermaid rejects an empty quoted description.

Transition selection and graph analysis do not change.

Fixes #1336.
title: fix(foldkit): escape arbitrary tags in Machine Mermaid output

Six published packages declared an engines.node range that accepts Node versions a package they run with rejects. @foldkit/ui, @foldkit/devtools, and @foldkit/devtools-mcp declared >=18.0.0 while requiring a foldkit that needs >=20.19.0. @foldkit/markdown and @foldkit/vite-plugin require Vite 8, which needs ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0, but declared >=18.0.0 and >=20.19.0. @foldkit/oxlint-plugin declared >=20.19.0 || >=22.12.0, a copy of the Oxlint range with the caret lost. Add a check:engines gate that runs on every CI build. It fails when a published workspace package has no Node range, has a clause that another single clause already covers, or accepts a Node version that one of its dependencies or required peers rejects. Oxlint is not a dependency of the plugin, so for that package the gate catches the lost caret but does not compare against Oxlint itself.

Fixes #904.
title: fix: align published Node engine ranges with required packages

A left mouse press on a `Popover`, `Menu`, or `Listbox` trigger records `maybeLastButtonPointerType` as `'mouse'`, and `update` ignores blur while that value is `'mouse'`. The `click` that ends the press clears it. Say the user drags off the trigger and releases somewhere else. The browser fires no `click` on the trigger, so the value stayed `'mouse'`, and the overlay ignored every later blur and stayed open when focus left it.

The trigger now dispatches `MovedPointerOffButton` when a mouse pointer leaves it, and `update` clears the recorded pointer type. If the pointer returns and the user releases on the trigger, the browser fires a `click`, and that click toggles the overlay.

A right or middle mouse press no longer records `'mouse'`. The browser fires no `click` on the trigger for those buttons. When the overlay is open and that press moves focus out of it, the overlay now closes.

Fixes #1494.
title: fix(ui): close an overlay on blur after a mouse press leaves the trigger

Escape in an open Menu inside a Popover panel closed the Menu and the Popover together. The Menu items handler called preventDefault, the keydown bubbled to the panel, and the panel handler dispatched RequestedClose for the same key press.

OnKeyDownPreventDefault, OnKeyDownSelfPreventDefault, and OnKeyDownFocus now return before they call the translator when the event already has defaultPrevented set. The first Escape closes the Menu and the second closes the Popover. A Listbox or Combobox inside a Popover panel, and a Menu inside a HoverIntent panel, get the same result. Dialog and the key bindings Subscription already skip a keydown with defaultPrevented set. OnKeyDown is unchanged and still dispatches for every keydown. OnKeyUpPreventDefault is out of scope: no container in @foldkit/ui claims a key on keyup that its content also claims.

The HoverIntent trigger claimed Escape even while its panel was closed. With the new rule, that trigger inside a Popover panel would have kept Escape from the Popover. It now returns Some for Escape only while the panel is open, as Tooltip already does.

Scene.keydown records preventDefault on its simulated event, so two claiming handlers on one element dispatch once in a Scene, as they do in the browser.

This is breaking: when two of these handlers return Some for the same key, only the first one now dispatches. The changeset shows how to keep the second one with OnKeyDown.

title: fix(foldkit)!: leave a claimed keydown to the handler that claimed it

Calendar.toDateLocal passed the year to the Date(year, monthIndex, day) constructor. That constructor reads a year from 0 to 99 as 1900 to 1999, so Calendar.toDateLocal(Calendar.make(50, 3, 1)).getFullYear() returned 1950. February 29 of year 0 came back as March 1, 1900, because 1900 is not a leap year.

The function now sets a Date to local midnight and then sets the year, month, and day with setFullYear, which takes the year as written. The returned Date has the year of the CalendarDate. For every other year the result is the same as before.

Fixes #1499.
title: fix(foldkit): keep years 0 to 99 in Calendar.toDateLocal

A query field whose encoded form is an array, such as `Schema.Array(Schema.String)`, built one comma-joined parameter (`?tags=rent%2Clease`). Parsing read one string for each key, so the array Schema rejected that URL and the link opened the not-found route.

`Route.query` now reads the encoded side of a `Schema.Struct` to find its array fields. Such a field builds one parameter for each element (`?tags=rent&tags=lease`) and parses every value of that parameter back into the array. An empty array builds no parameter. When the URL has no parameter for an array field, a required field parses to an empty array and an optional field parses as a missing key. Every other field builds and parses as before, and that includes a field that accepts a string or an array.

Fixes #1498.
title: fix(foldkit): round-trip array fields in Route.query

body:
A Calendar focus move first clamps the target to minDate and maxDate, then walks past disabled dates in the direction of the move. When the clamped date was itself disabled, that walk ran out of the allowed range, found nothing, and fell back to the clamped date. With maxDate on a Saturday and weekends disabled, ArrowRight from the Friday before it put focus on the Saturday, where Enter selects nothing.

The search now walks back the other way when the first walk finds no enabled date. A key press that has nowhere to go leaves focus where it is. A longer key move that reaches past the boundary, such as PageDown, lands on the last enabled date before it. When neither walk finds an enabled date, a key press leaves the Model unchanged.

The previous-month and next-month buttons and the month and year grids change the view month, so they accept the date from the walk back only when it is in the month they show. Otherwise focus stays on the clamped date, as before.

Fixes #1493.
title: fix(ui): keep Calendar focus off a disabled min or max date

An open @foldkit/ui Dialog that was removed together with its page kept the page scroll locked and kept its document keydown handler, focus trap, return focus, and stack entry. The Dialog released those resources only when update handled the Unmounted Message. When the same update removes the Model that owns the Dialog, Update.foldChild reads no child Model and drops that Message, so ReleaseDialogResources never ran. The AcquireResources Mount did not help, because a Dialog opened after its element mounted never starts that Mount.

Dom.showDialog now observes the document while a dialog is open. When an open dialog element is no longer connected, it calls Dom.releaseDialogResources for that id. The release no longer depends on a Message that reaches update. An element that moves to another parent in the document stays connected and keeps its resources. The Unmounted Message still resets a Model that survives.

The OnUnmount and Dialog RenderInfo docs now say that the Message reaches update only while the Model that handles it exists. The Dom page and the showDialog TSDoc tell the caller to call lockScroll once for each showDialog that resolves to true, because the release includes one page scroll lock.

Fixes #1482.
title: fix(foldkit): release an open dialog when its element is removed

DevTools evicts history one keyframe segment at a time. It dropped `keyframeInterval` entries and moved the history start forward by the same amount without checking how many entries it held. With `maxEntries` below the interval, such as `devTools: { maxEntries: 20 }` and the default interval of 31, the first eviction moved the start to 31 after only 21 Messages. The retained entries got indices that skipped ahead, no snapshot existed at the new start, and reading a retained index through time travel or the MCP `foldkit_get_model_at` and `foldkit_diff_models` tools died with `getOrThrow called on a None`.

The DevTools store now caps the interval at half of `maxEntries`. A full segment always fits inside the retained entries, so a snapshot exists at the new start, and an eviction keeps at least half of the history. A cap at `maxEntries` alone would leave a single entry after the first eviction. The cap covers the default interval and an explicit `keyframeInterval` above the limit. With the defaults (100 entries, an interval of 31) nothing changes.

Fixes #1481.
title: fix(foldkit): cap DevTools keyframeInterval at half of maxEntries

An open Menu or Listbox treated every single-character key as typeahead. Cmd+F added "f" to the search query and the keydown handler called preventDefault, so the browser's find shortcut never ran. Ctrl+C, Cmd+R, and every other shortcut built on a character key were blocked the same way.

Typeahead now takes a character only when Ctrl, Meta, and Alt are all up. A character keydown with one of them held produces no Message, so the browser keeps its default. That holds on the items panel and on the button while the panel is open. Space pressed with one of them also produces no Message: it is not typed into a pending query and it does not select the active item, so a chord such as Ctrl+Space, which switches the input method on some systems, cannot pick an item by accident. Shift still searches, since it only changes which character the key types.

Fixes #1491.
title: fix(ui): leave modifier shortcuts out of Menu and Listbox typeahead

A Mount on an element inside an anchored panel runs before the Mount on the panel, because snabbdom calls `insert` hooks for descendants first. The panel Mount then moves the panel into its portal root, and a browser resets the scroll offsets of an element that moves and of every element inside it. A list that a Mount scrolled to the selected row inside a Popover panel was back at the top once the panel opened.

`portalToContainingRoot` and `portalBackdrop` now read the scroll offsets of the element and its descendants before the move and restore them after it. `anchorSetup` portals through `portalToContainingRoot`, so Popover, Menu, Listbox, Combobox, and Tooltip panels get the same behavior. The restore uses `behavior: 'instant'`, so an element with `scroll-behavior: smooth` does not animate back to its offset.

The Anchor page now says that a Mount inside the panel runs before the panel is portaled, that scroll offsets survive the move, and that a Mount which measures position must defer by a frame.

Fixes #1492.
