body:
A routed app could not put the reader back where they were on Back, Forward, or reload, because update never learned that a URL change was a history traversal, and no entry carried an identity to key a scroll position by.

`routing.onUrlChange` now receives a `UrlChangeType` after the URL: `Push`, `Replace`, or `Traverse`. A routing `init` receives a `LoadType` after the URL: `Push`, `Reload`, or `Traverse`. Only the first routing `init` in a page receives `Reload` or `Traverse`. Each union has only the variants its entry point can receive. `Reload` and `Traverse` carry `maybeSavedScrollPosition`, an optional `ScrollPosition` holding the window position the reader last had on that entry. The server render passes `LoadType.Push()`, and the `foldkit/experimental/server` routing config types gain the parameter.

The runtime only reports. It never scrolls the window and never changes `history.scrollRestoration`. `pushUrl` and `replaceUrl` write a Foldkit entry key to `history.state`. The runtime keys the initial entry and any other entry without a key once it next reads it, and it detects when another script moved the reader to a new entry, so that entry never inherits the previous entry's key. Recorded positions, at most 100, are saved to `sessionStorage` on `pagehide` and when the runtime stops, without overwriting positions other documents in the tab saved since. While a browser restore may still be pending, from boot or a traversal until one frame after the render that shows the arrived entry, the runtime does not read the scroll position, so an app that ignores the new argument scrolls exactly as before.

Code that calls a typed routing `init` or `routing.onUrlChange` directly must pass the new argument. The routing guide gains a Scroll Position section, the Init & Flags page names the `LoadType`, and the Server Rendering page names the `LoadType` and the parts of the URL a static build cannot know. The website, the routing, personal blog, and SSG examples, and the `create-foldkit-app` SSG template adopt the pattern, restoring the position on Back, Forward, and reload, so a new app from the SSG template or the `routing` starter (`create-foldkit-app --example routing`) starts with it. The website and the examples compare routes to decide when to scroll to the top and keep the URL, including its query, out of the first Model, so a hydrated app's server and browser build the same first Model.

Closes #1511. Closes #812.
title: feat(foldkit)!: report how the reader arrived at a history entry

Adds a `schemaCompiler` option to `@foldkit/vite-plugin`. During `vite build` it compiles the Schemas exported by the listed modules with Effect's unstable `SchemaAOTCompiler` and installs the compiled parsers before the app's entry runs. App code does not change; the dev server and server builds keep interpreting.

```ts
foldkit({
  schemaCompiler: {
    modules: ['/src/schema/api.ts'],
    operations: ['decode', 'encode'],
  },
})
```

Listed modules are loaded in Node at build time, so they must not touch the DOM or start the Runtime, and must build the same Schemas as in the browser.

Measured on one desktop machine (production build, headless Chromium 153; allocation in Node 26):

| Operation | Interpreted | Compiled | Allocated per call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Decode a 1,000-item API response | 1.41 ms | 0.14 ms | 1.1 MB → 214 KB |
| Encode the same response | 1.37 ms | 0.14 ms | 1.1 MB → 212 KB |
| `Schema.is` on the same response | 1.35 ms | 0.09 ms | 1.1 MB → 2 KB |
| Decode 1,000 WebSocket frames (union) | 0.44 ms | 0.11 ms | 223 KB → 162 KB |
| Decode one small struct | 288 ns | 60 ns | 92 B → 82 B |

Bundle cost: about 1.6 KB gzipped for the compiler runtime plus generated code per Schema. The Kanban example with three Schemas grows by 4.5 KB gzipped (4%).

body:
`h.Style` takes strings, so a view that computes a style value formats the number itself, usually with a template literal, and JavaScript prints floating-point results in full: `${0.3 + index * 0.08}s` at index 2 renders `0.45999999999999996s`. A Scene test that asserts `'0.46s'` fails unless it copies the view's formatting. The same noise reached the DOM from `@foldkit/ui`, where the VirtualList, Toast, DragAndDrop and Anchor wrote values such as `0.30000000000000004px`, the edge-aligned Slider wrote fractions such as `0.3333333333333333` into `calc()`, and the Slider, Meter and Progress shared a two-decimal percentage helper. An animated value also had no simple way to limit style writes, since the style module skips a write only when the string is identical.

Add `foldkit/css`, exported as the `Css` namespace on `foldkit`, with one function per unit mirroring the numeric factories of CSS Typed OM: `number`, `percent`, `px`, `em`, `rem`, `ch`, `vw`, `vh`, `vmin`, `vmax`, `fr`, `deg`, `rad`, `turn`, `s` and `ms`. Each returns a plain string with at most four decimal places, trailing zeros removed and `-0` written as `0`, so `Css.s(0.3 + 2 * 0.08)` is `'0.46s'`. An optional `step` rounds to the nearest multiple first, like CSS `round(nearest, value, step)`, so values that render the same string cause no style write. A value that is not finite, an invalid step and a rounded result that is not finite each throw an `Error` starting with `[foldkit] Css.<name>`.

Move the numeric style values built at runtime in `@foldkit/ui` and in Foldkit's scroll lock onto `Css`, which `@foldkit/ui` imports from `foldkit/css`. The shared percentage helper formats with `Css.percent`, and the edge-aligned Slider writes its `calc()` fraction with `Css.number`. The Slider in both orientations, the Meter and the Progress now write percentages to four decimal places instead of two (`33.3333%`), the edge-aligned Slider's `calc()` fraction is written to four decimal places instead of every digit (`0.3333`), fractional values elsewhere lose their noise, and integers render as before. `h.Style`, the style module and `toHaveStyle` are unchanged.

Invalid `@foldkit/ui` input that used to fail silently now fails loudly. Any numeric input that makes a Slider, Meter, determinate Progress or VirtualList compute a length or percentage that is not finite now makes the view throw, and the render stops, instead of rendering `NaN%`, `NaNpx`, `Infinitypx` or `calc((100% - 0.75rem) * NaN)`, which the browser dropped. Any positioning input that makes the Anchor resolve a position or size that is not finite now makes it log `[@foldkit/ui] anchorSetup could not position the panel` and keep the visibility its caller rendered, where it used to write `NaNpx` or `Infinitypx` and still show the panel. For example:

- Slider, Meter and determinate Progress: a `value` of `NaN` with a non-empty range, a `min` or `max` of `NaN`, or a `min` of `-Infinity`.
- VirtualList: a `rowHeightPx` of `0`, `NaN` or `±Infinity`, or an `itemToRowHeightPx` that returns `NaN` or `±Infinity` for any item, including one that is off screen.
- Anchor: an `anchor.padding` of `NaN` or `±Infinity`, a Popover `arrowPadding` of `NaN`, or an `anchor.gap` or `anchor.offset` of `±Infinity`.

An `anchor.gap` or `anchor.offset` of `NaN` is unaffected, since Floating UI treats it as `0`. A throw while the Anchor applies a resolved position now reaches its existing once-per-run error report instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection.

Raise `@foldkit/ui`'s `foldkit` peer floor from `>=0.165.0` to `>=0.167.0`, in its `package.json` and in the peer floor check, because it now imports `foldkit/css`. Add a CSS Values docs page and link it from the `toHaveStyle` row of the Scene testing page.

Closes #1443
title: feat(foldkit,ui): add Css unit functions for numeric style values

body:
A createLazy or createKeyedLazy cache hit returns the VNode object the previous tree still holds. When an ancestor was re-keyed, changed tag, or switched branches, or the cached subtree moved into another parent, the differ reached createElm with that object and overwrote its elm with the new element. removeVnodes then ran the outgoing tree's destroy hooks on the same object, so they read the new element. The old Mount was never released while a second one started, the event-listener module removed the listener from the new button, and a subtree moved into an earlier sibling was removed from its new parent.

Add claimVNodeForCreate to the differ. A VNode whose elm is undefined passes through unchanged. One that already owns an element is copied with elm and the event-listener module's listener cleared, data shared, and its children copied the same way. Every createElm entry point claims the VNode first and writes the result back into the slot it came from: the element and fragment child loops, addVnodes, the three new-node paths in updateChildren, and the root replacement in patch, which now returns the claimed root and passes it to onRootPatched. On the next render the cached VNode is diffed once against the copy and takes the DOM back without rebuilding the view.

A same-position cache hit still short-circuits at oldVnode === vnode, and fresh trees are created without copying.

Fixes #1439
title: fix(foldkit): create DOM from a copy of VNodes that already own elements

Adds `deno` as a package-manager choice, so a scaffolded project can install, build, typecheck, and serve without a Node.js runtime.

```bash
npx create-foldkit-app@latest --package-manager deno
```

## Three things Deno does differently

**The scaffold's own install waives the dependency-age check.** Deno refuses an npm package published in the last 24 hours by default, and the manifest the CLI just wrote names the registry's `latest`. A Foldkit release earlier the same day therefore left `deno install` with no version satisfying the manifest, and it failed outright:

```
error: Could not find npm package '@foldkit/devtools' matching '^0.148.1'.
```

`installArgs` passes `--min-dep-age=0` for that one install. The generated `deno.json` keeps Deno's default, and the lockfile written by that install means a later plain `deno install` resolves nothing again.

**`build.mjs` names the vite shim by path.** `deno task` does not put `node_modules/.bin` on PATH, so a bare `vite` spawn from inside the script finds nothing. A bare `npm:vite` specifier resolves to whatever the registry calls latest and lands in the lockfile as `npm:vite@*`, which would run vite 9 in the build while the dev server and vitest stayed on vite 8. Naming `node_modules/.bin/vite` keeps the build on the version the project pins.

**The SSG scaffold drops `tsx`.** It runs `prerender.ts` directly under `deno run`.

## One host, two platform wirings

The SSR request handling moves to `server/handler.ts`. `server/main.ts` keeps only the platform wiring, and a Deno scaffold replaces that file and nothing else — 22 lines instead of a 200-line duplicate. Both hosts answer requests through one set of rules rather than each carrying a copy free to drift.

Overlays live in `templates/rendering-overlays/` rather than under `templates/package-managers/`. Both `package-managers/<pm>/` and `rendering/<mode>/` are copied wholesale into a project, so an SSR overlay parked in either one is written into scaffolds it does not apply to — a Deno SPA was shipping a server host it had no dependency for.

## Gate

`check-scaffold-server-rendering` now runs its SSR and SSG legs under npm **and** under Deno. The Deno leg asserts the dependency swap (`@effect/platform-deno` at the Node package's pinned version), the overlay, the absence of stray template paths, `deno task typecheck`, a build on the pinned vite, and then the same host-policy and Chromium hydration probes the Node host already faces. It installs this workspace's `foldkit` and vite plugin over the published ones by replacing Deno's store entries, since Deno has no equivalent of `npm install <tarball>`.

CI installs Deno and passes `--require-deno`, so a missing toolchain fails the gate instead of quietly shrinking what it covers. A local run without Deno says what it skipped.

Every assertion was mutation-checked — broken, watched fail, restored:

| Mutation | Caught by |
| --- | --- |
| `--min-dep-age=0` dropped | `deno install` — "Could not find npm package" |
| `'npm:vite'` restored | "lockfile records `["npm:vite@*"]`" |
| Overlay moved under `package-managers/deno/rendering` | "contains a rendering/ directory" |
| Platform swap removed | "still depends on @effect/platform-node" |
| Node types reference deleted | `deno task typecheck` — `TS2591: Cannot find name 'node:path'` |
| Overlay given its own handler copy | "does not import its handler… can drift" |
| Deno off PATH with `--require-deno` | hard fail |
| Deno off PATH without it | loud skip, then pass |

## Two fixes the gate itself needed

The host-failure diagnostic read `output()` the moment `exitCode` was set, racing the process's final write — the first Deno failure reported an empty reason. `RunningHost` now carries a `flushed` promise the diagnostic waits on.

The gate marks its local manifest by rewriting `effect` to `=<version>`. npm accepts that as an exact range; Deno installs and builds with it, then `deno run` refuses the built server with `Invalid package specifier 'npm:effect@=...'`. The Deno manifests carry a verbatim pin, and the npm leg still asserts the manifest directory is read.

## Verification

Deno and Node SSR hosts answer identically on `GET /`, a client-route deep link, a missing hashed asset, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, and `POST` — same statuses, same `cache-control` / `vary` / `x-content-type-options`, same four `data-foldkit-*` stamps, same byte count.

Full `pre-push` suite green, plus the extended gate passing both legs.
title: feat(create-foldkit-app): add deno package manager

Implements the lowering half of #622. No new MCP tool or WebSocket protocol message (the `foldkit_export_session` / `foldkit session export` surface that *emits* the artifact is explicitly out of scope for this PR).

## What

`Story.fromSession(artifact, { Model, Message })` lowers a captured session artifact into the steps of a runnable regression `Story`. Splice it straight into the existing runner:

```ts
Story.story(update, ...Story.fromSession(artifact, { Model, Message }))
```

An artifact is the minimal, self-describing shape the issue proposes: the initial Model plus an ordered log of entries, each carrying a dispatched Message, the Commands it triggered, and the resulting Model snapshot. It decodes with `Schema` (no raw `JSON.parse`), and reuses the devtools `SerializedCommand` shape for the triggered-Command list rather than inventing a parallel format. New exports from `foldkit/test`: `Story.fromSession`, plus `Story.SessionArtifact` / `Story.SessionEntry` Schemas and the `Story.SessionSchemas` type.

## Why it replays deterministically

Per the effect-result nuance in the issue: a Command's outcome already shows up in the log as its own later Message entry. So the lowering walks the entries in order and, for each one, either

- dispatches the Message as fresh input (`Story.message`), or
- when Commands from earlier entries are still pending, resolves the oldest pending Command with this entry's Message — exactly what `Story.Command.resolve` consumes.

The recorded outcomes come from the log, so replay is deterministic even though the original effects were not. Every entry also asserts the replayed Model against its recorded snapshot (via `Equal.equals`), so the generated story fails the moment replay drifts from the capture.

## Tests

Hand-authored artifacts in the devtools wire shape, driven through the counter test app:

- a pure-Message sequence (no Commands);
- a Command whose result Message appears in a later entry (asserts the resolve wiring + the post-resolve Model), including the args-matching variant;
- an intermediate-snapshot drift that the generated story catches;
- a triggering Command with no following result entry (surfaces as `Story`'s existing unresolved-Command error);
- a structurally malformed artifact and an entry whose Message does not match the app Message Schema (both clean `Schema` decode errors).

Full `foldkit` suite green (1463 passing) and `tsc --noEmit` clean; changeset is `minor` (additive test API).

## What remains for the end-to-end loop

This PR is the `foldkit/test` bridge only. To close the capture→fixture loop, a follow-up needs the export surface that emits the artifact from a live session (`foldkit_export_session` MCP tool and/or a `foldkit session export` CLI over the existing WS bridge), including the exporter's job of correlating each triggered Command to the result-Message entry it produced. The current lowering pairs pending Commands to result entries positionally (FIFO), which is exact for the common linear session; richer correlation metadata from the exporter could later disambiguate interleaved/concurrent effects.
title: feat(test): Story.fromSession — lower a captured session into a regression Story

Example wiring for #613. Opened as a draft starting point; happy for you to take it the rest of the way (changeset copy, knip allowance for the plugin devDep, whether the preset belongs in base vs a shared frontend tsconfig).

## What this does

- Adds `@effect/language-service` to `tsconfig.base.json → compilerOptions.plugins` with a browser/TEA `diagnosticSeverity` preset.
- Adds `@effect/language-service` as a root devDependency.
- Adds `docs/effect-language-service.md` (preset rationale + the tsserver-vs-CI patch note).
- Adds an empty changeset.

## Preset

Env rules (`processEnv`, `processEnvInEffect`) are `off` since browser apps read config via `import.meta.env`, not `process.env`. `preferSchemaOverJson` is a warning. `ignoreEffectWarningsInTscExitCode` + `ignoreEffectSuggestionsInTscExitCode` are `true`, so only Effect **errors** (e.g. a floating Command) affect the `tsc` exit code.

## Safety

The plugin surfaces in tsserver (editors) automatically. `tsc`/CI only load it after `effect-language-service patch`, which this PR does not add to the CI flow, so `pnpm -r typecheck` behaves exactly as before. Pure editor-DX gain until you decide to activate it in CI.

## Verification

Smoke-tested in a twin setup (a separate Foldkit app on the same `effect@4.0.0-beta.88` with `@effect/language-service@0.86.4` and this exact preset): `overview` resolves the full Foldkit Effect surface across all files, and a patched `tsc --noEmit` flags a floating Command as `error TS3: This Effect value is neither yielded nor used in an assignment`. A full monorepo verify (install + patch + `pnpm -r typecheck`) is left to CI.
